entity: The International Institute of Social History (IISH; Dutch Internationaal Instituut voor Sociale Geschiedenis, IISG), Amsterdam, founded in 1935 by Nicolaas Posthumus, since 1979 an institute of the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences (KNAW) in its Humanities Cluster: an archive and research institute of social history, the history of labour and social movements, and a data centre on socio-economic history, its collections the property of, or on standing loan to, the independent IISH Foundation; formalized in the maryleelabor left-and-labor census record of 2026-10-31 (https://www.maryleelabor.org/aggregators/iish/)

classes_note: Four classes, each stated by field sources at the loci given and, where the census states it, the census's own area, kind, evidence kind or record object for the entity: (1) archives of labour and social movements (census areas 'archives-and-custody' and 'movement-documents', evidence_kind 'archival collection', record.keeps; B1, B2, B3, B4, B5); (2) the papers and manuscripts of Marx, Engels and the socialist and anarchist movements (B2, B4, B6); (3) endangered archives rescued from seizure (B2, B4; not a census field); (4) socio-economic history data (census kind and record_object; B1). The aliases are the entity's English and Dutch names, its abbreviations IISH and IISG (case-sensitive), and its hosts (iisg.amsterdam, iisg.nl, socialhistory.org). The Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences (KNAW), its Humanities Cluster, the IISH Foundation, the Netherlands Economic History Archive (NEHA), the ESSHC and Nicolaas Posthumus are entities distinct from the institute (its academy, its cluster, the owner of its collections, an archive it houses, a conference it organizes, its founder); none is an alias. #1725, the census's anchor, is read at the passages that name the kind (the organ, the holder and the route by which a defeated critique is carried forward; the Hague expulsion of 1872; the critique that no one holds): its 'holder' is a role in an organization, and the census's ml_reading ('a holder in #1725's sense') is the archive's reading, ledgered as ML-NN, not a class. Admission by reading (§3.4): D where a deposit names the institute and says something of it; O-class where a sentence applies an archive category to one of the four classes; a bare mention, a reference line, a URL or a list of keywords is not a claim.
